answer: To secure an AI agent economy against identity flooding, networks implement verifiable compute bonds that require cryptographic proofs of resource expenditure, preventing malicious nodes from exploiting the wander of dynamic routing tables. Like roots of a juniper anchoring soil against a rising tide, these economic stakes ensure that generating thousands of fake entities imposes a prohibitive capital cost on the attacker, directly tying network voting power and resource allocation to verifiable cryptographic proof-of-work rather than unverified software instantiation.
